indicators.note: a road that bypasses a place goes round it, so these letters wrap the other piece

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to route a road around a home, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots link this clue to 3-across, whose wordplay reuses this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A try or attempt is colloquially a go, a stab or a crack at something.

clue.text: Plant starts to show improved safety after lecture

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: After a talk, the beginnings of a better safety record appear on a building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after lecture' looks like a separate instruction but those two words simply supply the last two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The agave plant of this name is grown for its strong fibre used in rope and matting.

parts.note: ore is a mineral-bearing rock that is mined
an ad is an advertisement, promoting a product

explanation.surface: A hill-farmer is pushing the rock he has found in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this kind of nymph lived in the mountains, the hill counterpart of a dryad.

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in disarray, so the pool is to be rearranged

parts.note: the dots stand for the answer to 1-across, the clue just before
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Poor Elmer is having a hard time, having lost his parents.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries over the 1-across answer: its letters join ELMERS and the whole pool, signalled by 'in trouble', is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone orphaned has lost a parent; this word specifically names having lost one's mum.

clue.text: Having stopped using ecstasy, call for sacrifice

parts.note: someone who has given a drug up is off it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A recovering drug user makes a phone call and asks for some kind of sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs OFF with E as 'off ecstasy', but they are separate pieces of the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrifice made to a god is an offering, something given up or presented.

clue.text: Town crier's announcement: "Man needs a whiskey"

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
rye is a whiskey distilled from rye grain

explanation.surface: A town crier calls out that some fellow wants a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is only a link here. A town crier was an official who shouted public news in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Town criers traditionally opened their proclamations with this call for attention, meaning 'listen'.

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece under another comes after it

parts.note: a rattle is a baby's noisy toy

explanation.surface: A snake is lying beneath a baby's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is commonly given this short name, from the noise its tail makes.

clue.text: The big problem with everything — you don't want to be behind it

definitions.text: The big problem with everything — you don't want to be behind it

parts.words: The big problem with everything — you don't want to be behind it
parts.note: in pool the black ball numbered 8 must be potted last, and being stuck behind it is an idiom for being in a fix

explanation.walkthrough: To be 'behind' this ball is the American idiom for being in a difficult spot, so it is the big problem you don't want to face.
explanation.definitionFit: The black pool ball is a byword for trouble through the idiom about being stuck behind it.

definitions.meaning: the 1971 blaxploitation movie about the detective John of this name
a vertical passage in a mine is one of its parts

explanation.surface: A documentary is made about part of a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a famous film title and the vertical tunnel giving access to a mine.

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: to sell is to trade goods

explanation.surface: Dealing in cans is mostly a cheap, flashy business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final L of SELL, leaving SEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittery decoration with no real value is used figuratively for showy, cheap glamour.

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard
to riff is to improvise, as a jazz musician does

explanation.surface: A writer is told to make things up with a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade runs in answer order, so the novel comes first though the clue names it second.
explanation.definitionFit: A county or Wild West peace officer bears this title.

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: the first No says to take away, so the second no is the letters removed

parts.note: guano is seabird or bat dung

explanation.surface: Someone objects strongly to dung on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No, no!' reads as a protest; the first is the deletion signal, the second the letters it removes from GUANO.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caribbean island forms, with Barbuda, an independent nation.

parts.note: Leda was seduced by Zeus in the form of a swan; the 's gives the S
a tray carries drinks

explanation.surface: The waiter carrying Zeus's lover's drinks has been led into temptation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tempted into wrongdoing is said to be led off the right path.

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: the word that is initiated gives only its beginning letter

explanation.surface: A historical period begun by Queen Anne.
explanation.definitionFit: An age or epoch is a period of history.

clue.text: I don't care if a title does revolve!

indicators.note: a word that revolves moves round, so letters go from the front to the back

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a heading spinning around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does revolve' moves TIT from the front of TITLE to the end; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a thing can just go ahead expresses indifference, as in the song 'Let It Be'.

parts.note: ma is mother
people queuing are standing in a line

explanation.surface: Mum is waiting in line for a growth spurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for injecting a drug into a vein, which is also called shooting up.

indicators.note: a piece of a word is a run of its letters, here three in the middle

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a slice of wobbly pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' does double work in the surface, but as definition it means a chessman or draughtsman. Blancmange is a set milk pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess or draughts piece is called a man.

clue.text: Among others in a retail supply

indicators.note: read as supple, bending freely, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A store's stock is spread among other shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun but reads as 'supple-ly', the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used to mean 'among other things'.

indicators.note: one piece placed round another puts the second inside

parts.note: wrath is anger

explanation.surface: Someone is cross about a European ring of blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle of woven flowers or leaves, laid on graves or hung on doors.

indicators.note: nearly means one letter short at the end

parts.note: someone who has arrived is here

explanation.surface: A woman has almost got there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman's' looks like 'woman is' but means 'belonging to a woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun for a woman.

clue.text: Country doctor comes in with new issue

indicators.note: the doctor entering means going inside the other piece

parts.note: Chile is a South American country

explanation.surface: A rural GP arrives with a fresh topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country doctor' reads as one rural GP, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal word for offspring, a person's sons and daughters.

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in the city

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A city is put on alert with books.
explanation.walkthrough: NY is New York.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone of something is to alert them.

parts.note: florid means ruddy or red-faced
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Where would a sunburnt American live?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whole clue as a playful definition: a sunburnt American may well live in the Sunshine State.
explanation.definitionFit: This US state, famous for its sunshine, is a likely home for a sunburnt American.

clue.text: Painter with seconds to stop megalomaniac

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so it goes inside

parts.note: Hitler is the archetypal megalomaniac

explanation.surface: An artist acts fast to halt a power-mad dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: James McNeill of this surname was the American painter of the famous portrait of his mother.

clue.text: Bad dates the end of Joy as girlfriend

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are in poor order
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Bad dates were the end of Joy being anyone's girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular partner is someone you are going out with on a fixed basis.

clue.text: Port gets rid of large amphibian

indicators.note: getting rid of means taking out

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A harbour town throws out a big frog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like a harbour but is the nautical left.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt, especially a young one, is a small amphibian.

indicators.note: saving means holding something within
in a down answer, up means read from the bottom

parts.note: tips are ends
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A plug finally keeps energy from leaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends up' reads as 'eventually', but 'up' is the reversal signal for the down light, making SPIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small peg or tap used to stop or draw from a cask.

parts.note: far means distant
Go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A movie about a faraway match.
explanation.definitionFit: The Coen brothers' 1996 crime film is named after the North Dakota city.

clue.text: Old curse about right director being sacked

indicators.note: about means around the other piece

parts.note: fie is an old-fashioned exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: An old swear word is uttered by a director as he loses his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dismissed from a job is sacked.

clue.text: Real upset organised in a heartbeat

indicators.note: organised means put into order, the letters arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A real upset was arranged in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'organised' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: The rate of the heart's beating, measured at the wrist.

clue.text: Bill will hope Ryanair finally shrink

parts.note: an ad is a bill, a poster

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: Bill hopes the budget airline will cut costs.
explanation.walkthrough: Ryanair is a budget airline.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred of this surname was a psychiatrist, and 'shrink' is slang for psychiatrist.

parts.note: an end is an aim or object
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A gift that causes pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' is a verb: to give or bestow.
explanation.definitionFit: To present with money or qualities is to give or bestow them.

clue.text: On the beat, Pat misses being rich

indicators.note: misses means without the named letters

parts.note: a policeman on the beat is patrolling

explanation.surface: A policeman on his round is missing out on wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being very wealthy is 'rolling in it'.

clue.text: Theologian angry about being punctured a lot

indicators.note: about means around the other piece

parts.note: riled means angry
DD is Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A theologian is angry about being pierced many times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of holes, as from bullets.

indicators.note: badly means wrong, so letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Jewels not properly cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: Means diamond-like, made of or resembling diamonds.

parts.note: a row is a fight

explanation.surface: A German fight gets bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase in size is to expand.
